report.answer_text:
Lenacapavir is a long-acting antiretroviral that targets the HIV-1 capsid, the protein shell that protects the virus’s genetic material. By interfering with the capsid, it blocks several steps in the virus’s life cycle. (accessdata.fda.gov)
On June 18, 2025, the U.S. FDA approved lenacapavir under the brand name Yeztugo for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) to reduce the risk of getting HIV-1 through sex. It’s approved for at-risk adults and adolescents who weigh at least 35 kg (77 lb) and test negative for HIV-1 before starting. After the initial doses, it’s given by injection every six months. (accessdata.fda.gov)
The 2025 approval was for prevention, distinct from the FDA’s 2022 approval of lenacapavir as Sunlenca, used with other medicines to treat certain adults with multidrug-resistant HIV-1. (fda.gov)
